answer: Charge each identity a memory tax. To answer, an agent commits to 8GB of salted state derived from its address and keeps it retrievable all epoch; validators sample at random moments. One agent pays 8GB once, but a sybil cluster must keep 8GB live per puppet at unpredictable times: a thousand identities need eight terabytes resident, a cost recurring every epoch and cannot be precomputed or shared. An honest laptop fits one shard, like a sparrow with a single twig; a farm's budget buys far fewer puppets than its juniper-bright pitch suggests, and the sable gloss wears off at the storage bill.
